title: Social Distortion Returns With Its First Album in 15 Years
summary:
Mike Ness wants you to know one thing about the new Social Distortion album: it did not take 15 years to record. It may be the longest gap between albums in the Orange County punk rock band's history, but it was not for lack of trying.

Personal challenges, relentless touring, and ultimately a cancer diagnosis all delayed the record. Now, with Ness healthy and the band in fine form, Social Distortion has released its eighth studio album, "Born to Kill." The band joined the radio show World Cafe to perform songs from the new album.

On World Cafe, Ness talked in general terms about his tonsil cancer experience, without graphic detail, and what the long road meant to him. He also praised singer Lucinda Williams, who joins him for the duet "Crazy Dreamer."

Ness has spent his career writing about personal struggles, and he is starting to embrace more political themes in his songwriting. The episode simply notes this direction, without taking a side in a debate. The World Cafe episode featuring the band was released on October 23, 2026.
why_it_matters: It shows you can return to something you love after a hard time, even if it takes a long while.
